prompt: A discovered project meets every commerciality criterion with established technology. Its investment has been sanctioned and its wells are still being built. Which Reserves sub-class does the engine derive?
options: justified-for-development
approved-for-development
on-production
development-pending
explanation: The engine derives the sub-class from the two stated facts: decision taken and no production gives approved-for-development (PRMS 2.1.3.5.5, Table 1), the sub-class of Ekene infill wells (EKN-2). Justified-for-development is the step before, with no investment decision yet. On-production needs the project on production. Development-pending is a Contingent Resources sub-class and cannot apply to a commercial project.

prompt: The golden input class-justified states a commercial project with the final investment decision not taken and production not started. What sub-class does the engine return?
options: approved-for-development, since every commerciality criterion is met here
development-pending, as the decision is still to come
No sub-class until the investment decision is taken
justified-for-development: no final investment decision yet
explanation: With neither fact true the engine returns justified-for-development and prints the decision "justified-for-development: no final investment decision yet". Approved-for-development needs the decision taken. Development-pending belongs to Contingent Resources, and this project is commercial. The engine always returns a sub-class for a Reserves project; the missing decision is what sets this one.

prompt: For a project it finds commercial, which two stated facts does the engine read to derive the Reserves sub-class?
options: Whether the final investment decision is taken and whether the project is on production
The reserves status and the stated economic status of the project
The years to the start of development and whether a longer wait is justified
Its chance of development and whether the firm intention to proceed is stated
explanation: The Reserves sub-class is derived from the project status: finalInvestmentDecision and onProduction, each a stated true or false (PRMS 2.1.3.5, Table 1). The reserves status is stated for Reserves and checked against the project status; it sets no sub-class. The start and its justification set the time-frame criterion, which decides the class. A Reserves project carries no chance at all, and the firm intention is a commerciality fact.

prompt: Ekene Main waterflood (EKN-1) is stated as on production. In a copy of it the final investment decision is set to false. What does the engine return?
options: The sub-class justified-for-development, read from the missing decision
On-production, as production outranks it
A refusal naming projectStatus.finalInvestmentDecision
A refusal naming subClass, which must change to approved-for-development
explanation: A producing project has passed its investment decision, so the engine refuses the contradiction in the facts and names the fact to fix: "projectStatus.finalInvestmentDecision must be true for a project on production (a producing project has passed its investment decision); got false". It derives no sub-class from facts that disagree, so neither justified-for-development nor on-production comes back, and the refusal names the decision field, since the sub-class check never gets that far.

prompt: Ekene infill wells (EKN-2) has its investment decision taken and is not on production. In a copy, the reserves status is changed to developed-producing. What happens?
options: The call returns developed-producing as stated, since the reserves status is a stated fact the engine records
The sub-class moves up to on-production to match the stated reserves status
The call is refused on reservesStatus, which must be developed-non-producing or undeveloped
The call is refused on subClass, which must then read on-production
explanation: Developed producing reserves come from completion intervals open and producing (PRMS 2.1.3.6, Table 2), so the engine refuses on reservesStatus and names the two statuses a project not on production may carry. The status is stated and it is also checked. The engine never moves a sub-class to fit a status; the sub-class follows the project status, and here the project is not on production.

prompt: How does the engine set the sub-class of a Contingent Resources project?
options: It takes the stated one and checks only that it is one of the four
It derives it from the list of blockers that the commerciality test names for the project
It reads it from the stated economic status of the project
It derives it from the stated chance of development, Pd
explanation: The engine cannot see why a development is waiting, so the Contingent sub-class is stated and checked against the four of PRMS 2.1.3.5.6 and Table 1: development-pending, development-on-hold, development-unclarified and development-not-viable. The blockers and the economic status are printed beside it, and the chance of development sets the chance of commerciality; none of them sets the sub-class.

prompt: In a copy of Ekene East gas (EKN-3), the stated sub-class development-on-hold is changed to development-not-viable, and nothing else moves. What does the engine return?
options: A refusal: the not-viable sub-class needs a not-viable economic status
Contingent Resources, with the sub-class reset to development-on-hold
Discovered Unrecoverable, since no project is planned for it any more
Contingent Resources, sub-class development-not-viable (stated)
explanation: The engine accepts any of the four Contingent sub-classes on any Contingent project, so it returns the class with development-not-viable as stated and the same six blockers. Nothing ties the sub-class to the economic status, and the engine never rewrites a stated input. Discovered Unrecoverable needs no recovery project at all, and EKN-3 states one with established technology. Whether the sub-class fits the blockers is a judgement left to the person who signs the report.

prompt: The appraisal project EKN-4, already discovered, carries a stated Pd of 65.000000 percent. Which Pc appears in its decisions?
options: No figure for a discovered project
65.000000 percent, from Pc = Pd
50.000000 percent, as Ekene East gas
A refusal until a Pg is stated first
explanation: A discovered project has already met its geology, so its chance of commerciality is the chance of development alone (PRMS 2.1.3.3). The engine's decision line is "Pc = Pd = 65%". Only Reserves carry no chance. 50.000000 percent is EKN-3's Pd. A chance of geologic discovery on a discovered project is refused, so asking for one would be the error.

prompt: A copy of a Contingent project states chances.geologicDiscoveryPct as 50 beside its chance of development. Which field does the engine refuse?
options: chances.geologicDiscoveryPct, which applies to Prospective Resources only
chances, since a Contingent project may state no chance of any kind
chances.developmentPct, which must then fall to the product of both
subClass, which must change to prospect once Pg is stated
explanation: The engine's message reads "chances.geologicDiscoveryPct must be left out for a discovered accumulation (the chance of geologic discovery applies to Prospective Resources, PRMS 2.1.3.2); got 50". A Contingent project must state its chance of development, so the chances object is required. The engine computes Pc = Pd for it and multiplies nothing. The discovery status sets the class, and a stated chance never turns a discovered project into a prospect.

prompt: Ekene Shallow lead (EKN-7) states a chance of geologic discovery of 15.000000 percent and a chance of development of 70.000000 percent. What chance of commerciality does the engine return?
options: 15.000000 percent
70.000000 percent
10.500000 percent
20.000000 percent
explanation: For an undiscovered project the chance of commerciality is the product Pc = Pg x Pd (PRMS 2.1.3.3), and the engine returns 10.500000 percent for EKN-7. Pg alone ignores the chance of development if found; Pd alone is the discovered-project rule. 20.000000 percent is EKN-6, whose Pg of 25.000000 and Pd of 80.000000 give a different product.

prompt: The golden input class-pg-zero states a prospect with a chance of geologic discovery of 0 and a chance of development of 50.000000 percent. What does the engine return?
options: Undiscovered Unrecoverable, since nothing can ever be found at that chance of discovery
A refusal: a chance of geologic discovery must be above 0
Prospective Resources with a Pc of 50.000000, from Pd
Prospective Resources, sub-class prospect, with a Pc of 0.000000
explanation: The engine classifies the facts it is given: an undiscovered accumulation with a recovery project is Prospective Resources, and the product 0 x 50 gives a Pc of 0.000000. Unrecoverable needs no recovery project, and this one states established technology. A chance of 0 lies inside the accepted range from 0 to 100, so there is nothing to refuse. Pd alone is the rule for a discovered project.

prompt: A copy of an undiscovered project states the sub-class development-pending. What does the engine return?
options: Contingent Resources, since the stated sub-class belongs to that class
The refusal: subClass must be one of "prospect", "lead", "play"; got "development-pending"
Prospective Resources with the stated sub-class printed beside it
A refusal on discovery, which must change to discovered first
explanation: Prospective Resources carry three stated sub-classes (PRMS 2.1.3.5.9, Table 1), and the engine checks the stated one is among them. The discovery status sets the class, and a stated sub-class never moves a project across the class line. The engine does not print a sub-class it has refused, and the discovery field is valid as stated, so the refusal names subClass.

prompt: On a commercial project with finalInvestmentDecision true and onProduction false, the box states subClass as development-pending. What does the refusal ask for?
options: One of the four Contingent Resources sub-classes, listed in full
A project status with both facts false, to fit development-pending
A chance of development for the pending project
The sub-class approved-for-development, which the facts give
explanation: The class is decided first, from the criteria, and this project is Reserves. The message reads "subClass must be "approved-for-development" for this project (final investment decision taken; production yet to start: PRMS 2.1.3.5.5, Table 1); got "development-pending"". The list of four Contingent sub-classes appears only when the facts make a project Contingent. The engine asks the stated sub-class to follow the facts, and a Reserves project carries no chance.

prompt: A project that fails six commerciality criteria states the sub-class approved-for-development. What does the engine do?
options: Refuses subClass, listing the four Contingent sub-classes and the six blockers
Classifies it as Reserves, since approved-for-development is a Reserves sub-class
Refuses projectStatus, since an approved project must state its decision
Returns Contingent Resources and prints the stated sub-class beside the blockers
explanation: A stated sub-class does not make a project commercial; the criteria do. The engine decides Contingent Resources first, then refuses: "subClass must be one of "development-pending", "development-on-hold", "development-unclarified", "development-not-viable" for Contingent Resources (not commercial: financialAppropriations, timeFrame, economicStatus, market, facilities, firmIntention)". A project status is read for Reserves alone, and the engine never returns a result that carries a sub-class from the wrong class.

prompt: A classification box carries the top-level key maturity beside the usual facts. What comes back?
options: The class and sub-class, with the unknown key dropped silently
A sub-class read from the maturity key in place of subClass
A refusal: maturity is not an accepted key, with the accepted top-level keys listed
A refusal naming subClass, which the maturity key hides
explanation: Every function checks its accepted keys before it reads a fact, and it drops nothing silently. The message reads "maturity is not an accepted key; the accepted keys at the top level are name, discovery, recoveryProject, subClass, commerciality, economicStatus, projectStatus, reservesStatus, chances, nigeria". The engine reads no key it does not know, so a maturity key is never read as a sub-class, and the key check runs before the sub-class check.
